findings.text: blocking: the landed change reddens an existing test — running that file at 82f3a3bdc gives 1 failed, 4 passed, and test_satisfied_section_wait_leaves_no_section_row raises on its `result["section_blocking"] == []` assertion with s3 held. The test encodes exactly the status reading this repair removes (a wait on s1 of a shipped plan that declares no section), while the roadmap's own rule at reckon/roadmap.py:1424-1430 is `found_section and _section_satisfied(...)`, which agrees with the landed change. The worker declared this under outside_scope and in the evidence fragment, and the file sits outside its write fence, so the coordinator must dispatch the expectation inversion before or with promotion; landing these two commits alone leaves main red.

non-blocking: _section_target_plan repeats a plan read the producer already performed on the same row in the same call chain — reckon/mcp.py:_resolve_plan_ref (reckon/mcp.py:1967) reads the target plan (through the same `None if external else checkout` scope expression duplicated at reckon/mcp_views.py:2654) and keeps only status/impl/title, so every section-scoped row in a read_plan summary now does two plan reads. The producer carrying the target's section_declarations (or its verdict) on the row would leave the readiness rule where it belongs and cost one read; the worker records the same shape under outside_scope.

non-blocking: the checkout threading the repair adds to resource_view (reckon/mcp_views.py:3257 and :3266, feeding _summary/_detail at :2902) has no guard. The new test calls _section_blocking directly with checkout=str(root), so a regression that dropped the provenance checkout would leave the test green while production fell back to the mounts-resolved checkout for local refs — silently reading another tree's plan copy. A second assertion through the read_plan/resource_view entry with a worktree checkout would close it.
